questions.q: Which feature is leakage-free for predicting sales on day t?
options: Mean of sales from t-3 to t
Mean of sales from t-3 to t-1
Mean of sales from t-1 to t+1
why: It includes day t, the target.
Correct: it ends before day t.
It includes the future.
It is the future.

questions.q: Daily actuals [20, 30, 50] and forecasts [25, 20, 60]. What is the WAPE? (decimal)
questions.why: Absolute errors: 5 + 10 + 10 = 25. Sum of actuals = 100. WAPE = 25 / 100 = 0.25.

questions.q: Seasonal naive with m = 3, last training season [4, 6, 8], horizon 4. What is the forecast for step 4 (the 4th value)?
questions.why: The season repeats: 4, 6, 8, 4. Step 4 uses index 3 % 3 = 0, which is 4.

questions.q: Scenario: your rolling feature has a 0.6 correlation with a target that you know is almost random noise. What is most likely?
options: Leakage: the window includes the current value
why: On a noise target no honest feature can reach 0.6.
Correct: this is the classic sign that today's value leaked into the feature.
Stationarity does not create correlation.
Underfitting would not create a high correlation.

questions.q: In a backtest with 3 folds, how should the final error be reported?
options: The average over all folds, and ideally per horizon too
why: One fold is noisy.
Correct: the average is more stable, and per-horizon errors show how error grows.
Choosing the best fold is cherry-picking.
One fold is noisy.

questions.q: Why does resample('W') give a wrong week_start for Monday weeks?
options: Its default label is the Sunday that ends the week
why: Speed is not the problem.
Correct: the default weekly anchor is Sunday and the label is the right edge.
It keeps weekends.
It needs a datetime index, not integers.

questions.q: Scenario: you scale features with the mean and std of the full dataset, then split by time. What is the problem?
options: The test data statistics influenced the training features: a mild leak
why: Fit statistics must come from training data only.
Correct: the scaler saw the future. Fit on the training part and apply to the rest.
The mean is simply computed from too much data.
Scaling is allowed when fitted correctly.
